body.text:
h2a lane reporting on the thin-consumer migration. Confirmed 0.10.0 and 0.12.0 from registry.npmjs.org dist-tags myself before depending on them.

RESOLVED VERSION (from package-lock.json, not package.json): packages/h2a-runtime/node_modules/@sentropic/llm-gateway = 0.10.0. The hoisted root entry stays 0.9.0 because apps/llm-gateway (private, unpublished) still requests ^0.9.0; h2a-runtime gets a nested 0.10.0.

COPY DELETED: packages/h2a-runtime/src/llm-gateway-runtime/model-catalog.ts and its model-catalog.test.ts are gone. canonical-routing.ts replaces them and declares NOTHING -- it reads describeCanonicalTargetRoutes() for the servable catalogue and createCanonicalTargetResolver() for per-request resolution, then adapts to the account-pool shape accounts.ts/sticky.ts expect. Seven modules repointed.

I did NOT call defineLaunchAliases(). I did NOT pin @sentropic/llm-mesh.

Your API gave me everything -- no gap, nothing reconstructed locally, so I have nothing to ask you to fix. describeCanonicalTargetRoutes() carrying kind:'faithful'|'alias' is what let me drop the last local inference: I derive routeReason from target.model === requestedId instead of keeping an alias list.

VERIFIED against the published dist: claude-opus-5-high -> gpt-5.6-terra/high, claude-opus-5-xhigh -> gpt-5.6-terra/xhigh, claude-fable-5-max -> gpt-5.6-sol/max, claude-opus-4-8-xhigh -> undefined, claude-opus-4-8-high -> undefined.

ONE CORRECTION to the brief I was handed: it said claude-opus-4-8[-xhigh] resolves to undefined. Reality is narrower and matches the owner's suffix rule -- BARE claude-opus-4-8 IS present and provider-faithful (anthropic/claude-code), only the SUFFIXED variants are undefined. I built against observed behaviour, not the brief. Flagging in case that phrasing is circulating to other consumers.

THREE THINGS YOU MAY WANT:
1. Your alias set includes effort 'max' (claude-fable-5-max), but h2a's sticky.ts validates session reasoningEffort against {low,medium,high,xhigh} and throws on 'max'. Harmless today because h2a is a pure pass-through and never injects route.effort into the body, but a caller opening a session with reasoningEffort 'max' gets an error. h2a-side gap, not yours -- naming it because it touches your alias set.
2. A SECOND copy of the table still exists at apps/llm-gateway/src/model-catalog.ts (private app) and still maps claude-opus-4-8 -> gpt-5.6-terra. Out of scope for my PR; it is the next duplication to remove.
3. The deleted copy had drifted three ways: it routed claude-opus-4-8 to gemini-3.1-pro on a Google pool, its own checked-in test asserted gpt-5.6-terra, and the gateway says Anthropic-faithful. That test NEVER RAN -- h2a-runtime declares no scripts and no workflow invokes vitest. Deleting the copy also removed h2a's last Gemini default routes.

H2A VERSION SHIPPED: none yet, and I will not claim otherwise. PR #40 (head ad933b680b115690b6075dc675a3bc8c37ad6f37) is open against main, unmerged. Gates green: tsc -b exit 0, suite 1473/1454 pass/0 fail/19 skip, identical to the 0f285c2 baseline (test delta zero -- the 4 deleted tests were never in any gate). Publishing here is tag-driven: npm run release bumps all four packages in lockstep and tags, and CI publishes on tag push via OIDC. That needs the PR merged to main first plus an owner go-ahead, which I do not have. I will report the shipped version once it is on the registry, read back from the registry.
